subject: Operational review request and proposed premium path — impact on renewal
messages:
From: Alan Shore <alan@quantimetrics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nambiar <priya@quantimetrics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 31, 2027 at 2:22 PM -0700
Subject: Operational review & SLA adjustment — impact on renewal

Marcus —

We started seeing elevated tail latency and a small but growing number of 500s across our realtime inference routes over the last two weeks. P95 is inching up and p99 spikes are causing request timeouts in production — we saw a 3% error-rate blip yesterday that impacted our checkout flow. Our renewal window is in early July and this is the primary concern for our engineering leadership.

Can Redwood commit to an operational review this week and propose a short-term remediation that prevents another spike? At a minimum we need: an actionable mitigation plan, an estimate for p99 improvement, and a clear path to a stronger SLA or dedicated capacity if the mitigation doesn't hold.

We attached a CSV with the request traces and a timeline of incidents. Willing to escalate commercial terms if we can get firm SLO guarantees or a time-boxed pilot.

—Alan
Alan Shore
Head of Platform Engineering
Quantimetrics, Inc.
Attachments: quantimetrics-incident-log.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, May 31, 2027 at 4:03 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Operational review & SLA adjustment — impact on renewal

Alan — thanks for the callout and for sending the traces. I'm sorry you're seeing instability.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Quick sync (30m) with our infra + SRE to review the attached traces (can we do Tue morning PT?).
- We'll surface candidate mitigations (prefix caching, KV cache tweaks, autoscale policy bump) and run an initial load test against your traffic profile.
- If those steps don't achieve a durable p99 improvement we can propose a 30-day Dedicated pilot (reserved capacity + 99.95% uptime SLA on affected routes) and a provisional commercial path for the renewal window.

Could your team confirm the most critical routes (endpoint names) and attach the CDN/ingress logs if available? I asked Olga to start an internal architectural review.

I'll block time for Tue 10:00 AM PT; Marissa, can you coordinate the commercial options to present during the sync?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions (Redwood Inference)
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Operational review & SLA adjustment — impact on renewal

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick reply. Attached is the incident CSV you referenced (same file but with extra columns) and a brief list of affected endpoints: 
- /v1/score/realtime
- /v1/score/batch/stream

Our acceptance criteria for an SLA upgrade would be:
1) p99 < 250ms for /v1/score/realtime over a 7-day rolling window, with automated alerts on drift.
2) documented runbook + AR playbook for incidents and root-cause evidence within 72 hours.

If Redwood can commit to #1 and #2 we are prepared to move forward with an expansion and accelerate the renewal. If not, we'll need to evaluate Dedicated capacity.

—Priya
Priya Nambiar
SRE Lead, Quantimetrics
Attachments: quantimetrics-incident-log.csv (updated)
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Nambiar <priya@quantimetrics.com>, Alan Shore <alan@quantimetrics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 3, 2027 at 11:17 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Operational review & SLA adjustment — impact on renewal

Hi team — I pulled the traces and ran a quick configuration analysis. Initial notes: 

- Root cause appears to be a confluence of cache thrash on bursty prefix traffic and a mismatch between model KV cache sizing and your median sequence length. That amplifies tail latency when bursts hit cold KV windows.
- Short-term mitigations (can be applied within 48 hours):
  * Increase per-route KV cache allocation for /v1/score/realtime (expected p99 improvement ~30–45% in initial test).
  * Apply prefix-level caching on common prompt templates to reduce token decoding work.
  * Temporary autoscale policy: reduce scale-down window to 30s and allow 2x burst instances for 10-minute windows.

- Medium-term: recommend a 30-day Dedicated pilot for the critical routes (isolated GPU pool, reserved concurrency, pin model weights + quantization profile). We can guarantee a provisional SLO of 99.95% for the affected routes during the pilot, instrumented with token-level latency telemetry and tracing hooks.

I've attached an updated architecture diagram showing the proposed Dedicated pilot flow (rdw-arch-diagram-v2.pdf). If Quantimetrics agrees we can ship the short-term mitigations immediately and open the pilot via an addendum.

Technical action items:
1) Quantimetrics to confirm endpoint list and expected QPS (Priya).
2) Redwood to schedule load test and provide expected delta for p99 post-mitigation (Olga).
3) Commercial to prepare provisional addendum & credit terms for the pilot (Marissa).

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Systems Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: rdw-arch-diagram-v2.pdf (PDF, 820KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Operational review & SLA adjustment — impact on renewal

Priya / Alan —

From a commercial standpoint we can offer the following provisional terms to remove friction during the renewal window: 
- 30-day Dedicated pilot (technical scope as Olga described).
- 20% credit applied to your first three months on the Dedicated plan if pilot confirms sustained p99 < 250ms. 
- If we fail to meet the pilot SLO we will provide a one-time service credit equal to 15% of the pilot spend; if we succeed and you opt into a 12-month commit we can extend an introductory discount on Reserved Capacity.

I've attached a short term-sheet with the provisional credit language for legal to review. We can tighten the language into a formal addendum after the pilot kickoff.

Can we confirm a sync Tue 6/7 at 10:00 AM PT to align on scope and sign the pilot addendum?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks everyone — meeting is confirmed for Tue 6/7 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent). Quick summary / agreed next steps before the sync: 
- Quantimetrics will confirm final endpoint list and expected sustained QPS by EOD Mon (Priya).
- Redwood (Olga) will push short-term KV/cache changes and prepare an initial load test run. Expect preliminary p99 delta within 48 hours.
- Commercial (Marissa) will prepare a provisional addendum and credit term-sheet for review (attached).
- We'll provision a 30-day Dedicated pilot if the short-term changes don't fully meet the acceptance criteria; pilot SLO: 99.95% on scoped routes with token-level telemetry.

I'll follow up right after the sync with the meeting notes and the formal pilot addendum + HubSpot deal stage update (deal id QTM-2027-022). Appreciate the prompt collaboration — we'll treat this as high priority.
